decision: Authorize Class A landing: which integration branch may Steward open repair PRs against, and may the scheduled workflow push steward/a/* branches and the steward/ledger ref?
whyItMatters: Class A repairs are proven in a throwaway checkout and stop there. Landing needs a target branch and contents/pull-requests write permission for the Steward workflow, which is a security-policy expansion only you can grant.
evidence: Landing refuses main/master/default branch in code; a target is configured only by GAIA_STEWARD_INTEGRATION_BRANCH or --integration-branch.
Without a target every Class A debt is recorded blocked: landing target not configured.
The shared ledger needs an unprotected refs/heads/steward/ledger that the Steward identity can fast-forward (never force).
recommended: Set repository variable STEWARD_INTEGRATION_BRANCH to a long-lived steward integration branch, set STEWARD_LANDING_ENABLED=true, and leave steward/ledger and steward/a/* unprotected.
alternative: Keep landing off: scheduled runs keep producing receipts and patches only, and a person applies Class A repairs by hand.
unblocks: Unattended Class A detect-repair-verify-PR without founder involvement; shared ledger for scheduled runs.
